blocks.text: Get Travel Nursing Opportunities in PEI

blocks.html:
Finding the right travel nursing job isn’t always easy. You want a place where your skills are valued, your time is respected, and your work makes a real difference.

There is a need to fill up healthcare staff in places such as Charlottetown, Summerside in Prince Edward Island. Hospitals, group homes, and clinics in both rural and urban settings urgently need nurses like you. 

These communities rely on compassionate professionals who can adapt fast, provide consistent care, and bring relief to overworked local staff.

At Goodwill Staffing, we connect qualified nurses with rewarding travel nursing opportunities across the island, ensuring healthcare organizations maintain stability while nurses gain flexible, well-paid contracts.

blocks.text: Why Does Travel Nursing Matter in Prince Edward Island?

blocks.html:
Like much of Canada, Prince Edward Island faces staffing shortages that directly impact patient care. 

Small hospitals and rural clinics often experience gaps when permanent staff take leave or when demand for care increases. 

Patients face longer wait times, and facilities struggle to maintain consistency without additional support.

Travel nursing provides the solution. Nurses who are ready to relocate temporarily bring immediate relief to facilities. This ensures patients receive the timely, safe, and compassionate care they deserve.

For nurses, travel assignments offer competitive wages, housing support, and the opportunity to build valuable experience in diverse care settings.

Travel nursing in Prince Edward Island is about keeping healthcare accessible, supporting frontline teams, and ensuring every community has the care it needs. And that’s where we play a key role as a staffing agency.

blocks.text: The Benefits of Travel Nursing in PEI

blocks.html:
Travel nursing is a career path that blends flexibility, growth, and lifestyle advantages.

Competitive pay packages: Travel nurses in PEI often receive higher hourly rates than permanent staff. Many assignments include housing stipends, travel allowances, or accommodation support.

Flexibility and variety: Nurses can choose contracts that align with their goals. Assignments can last from a few weeks to several months, giving nurses full control over their schedules.

Professional growth: By working across hospitals, community clinics, and long-term care homes, nurses gain broad experience that builds adaptability and confidence.

Island lifestyle: Beyond work, PEI offers beaches, festivals, fresh seafood, and a slower pace of life. For many nurses, it is the perfect mix of professional opportunity and lifestyle experience.

blocks.text: In-Demand Specialties for Travel Nurses in PEI

blocks.html:
Travel nurses are placed across the province in multiple healthcare settings:

  • Charlottetown: Home to Queen Elizabeth Hospital, the largest acute care facility in PEI. Travel nurses support emergency, surgical, medical, and critical care units.
  • Summerside: Community hospitals and family health clinics regularly require temporary nursing coverage.
  • Rural areas: Small towns and remote communities depend on travel nurses to ensure consistent access to healthcare services.
  • Long-term care facilities: Seniors’ homes across PEI rely on travel nurses to maintain continuity of care for residents.

Every placement is important. From acute care to community health, travel nurses keep services running smoothly across all regions of the island.

blocks.text: Where Are Travel Nurses Needed in Prince Edward Island?

blocks.html:
Healthcare facilities in PEI often request travel nurses with specific skills. Some of the most in-demand roles include:

  • Emergency Room (ER) Nurses: Handling urgent and critical cases.
  • ICU Nurses: Managing patients who require intensive monitoring.
  • Medical-Surgical Nurses: Providing care for post-op and general medical patients.
  • Long-Term Care Nurses: Supporting residents in seniors’ facilities.
  • Community Health Nurses: Delivering care in rural clinics and outreach programs.

Each specialty plays a vital role in keeping patient care safe, efficient, and accessible.

PEI travel contracts include premium pay, housing and travel coverage, and licensing support — so you can focus on the work that matters most.

For travel nurses, it’s a province that offers not just peace and simplicity — but purpose, belonging, and the kind of island pace that turns a contract into a calling.

blocks.text: Challenges Travel Nurses Help Solve in PEI

blocks.html:
Prince Edward Island’s healthcare system faces unique challenges, and travel nurses are essential in addressing them.

Staff shortages: With limited numbers of permanent staff, gaps in coverage are frequent. Travel nurses step in quickly to maintain staffing levels.

Rural access: Smaller communities outside Charlottetown and Summerside often struggle to attract permanent staff. Travel nurses make sure residents in these areas receive proper care.

Seasonal demand: During peak seasons, such as summer tourism or flu season, patient volumes increase. Travel nurses provide extra coverage to manage surges.

Continuity of care: Staff leaves, retirements, or sudden absences can disrupt services. Travel nurses provide seamless coverage to prevent interruptions.

blocks.text: Why Do Nurses Choose Travel Nursing in PEI?

blocks.html:
Travel nursing is an opportunity to build a rewarding career while experiencing life in a unique province. Nurses choose PEI for several reasons including:

  • Professional variety: Exposure to multiple care environments improves adaptability.
  • Stronger earnings: Travel packages often outpace traditional staff wages.
  • Supportive communities: Working in smaller healthcare settings means stronger teamwork and closer patient connections.
  • Lifestyle perks: Beaches, national parks, and cultural festivals make PEI an attractive location.

For many nurses, PEI provides a balance of career development and lifestyle enrichment.

items.answer: No. We help with travel and licensing support

items.question: Can I apply if I’m newly licensed or from another province?
items.answer: Candidates must have at least 2 years of relevant experience to be considered for PEI placements. We support interprovincial licensing and internationally educated professionals.

blocks.html: We help you navigate the provincial licensing process and reimburse licensing fees under select terms and conditions—so you can focus on getting started stress-free.
Travel RNs and LPNs in Prince Edward Island must hold an active nursing license and valid BLS certification. Make sure your documents are current and ready to upload.

All nurses in PEI are licensed through the College of Registered Nurses and Midwives of Prince Edward Island (CRNMPEI), which regulates both Registered Nurses (RNs) and Licensed Practical Nurses (LPNs).
You may also need to submit a vulnerable sector check, immunization records, and proof of insurance. Our team will guide you through every step.
Have questions about PEI nursing requirements? Our team can point you in the right direction and make sure you’re prepared for every step of the process.

Goodwill Staffing provides healthcare professionals with flexible contracts across Canada. We offer licensing support, paid housing, and placements in both coastal and rural communities for travel nurses.
